scope: follow the client object's address field
conclusion: the whole client object is untouched: every probed field, including the one the receive helper copies as a netadr and the one the game checks against 1 at 0x5B2B85, is zero. CL_Init allocated it and nothing else has ever written to it -- CL_Connect (or whatever fills cl) never ran.
meaning_for_the_route: raw-byte patching of cl is a dead end: the parser reads fields whose semantics depend on other zero fields, and writing them individually crashes
the only faithful way to get a filled cl is to run the game's own connect path
that path also explains why the server already reaches CS_ACTIVE: some other, lighter code sends the join packets while cl is left empty
next: locate CL_Connect in the binary (the function that writes clc.state and copies the server netadr) and find what UI action triggers it
two options: (a) call it from a runtime stub with the loopback address, (b) make the offline start path take the branch that calls it
option (b) is safer: it lets the game fill cl itself instead of us poking fields

code_search.pattern: mov eax,[0x331c0c8]; xor eax,0xD362501F; mov byte [eax],imm
code_search.note: the decoder in the connect path may use another register (ecx/edx) or a helper, so the exact pattern does not appear. Next attempts should match on the 0xD362501F xor site and inspect the following few instructions instead of requiring a byte store.
